The Federal Government has set an 18-month deadline for the completion of the National Library of Nigeria Headquarters in Abuja, following the revival of the long-abandoned construction project. The renewed construction was formally flagged off in Abuja after the Federal Executive Council approved the augmentation of the project contract in August 2026. The project, which commenced in 2006, suffered prolonged delays, leaving the headquarters unfinished for nearly two decades. In a post obtained from the federal ministry of education’s X handle on Friday, speaking at the ceremony, the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, disclosed that her 65th birthday fundraising appeal in December 2025 generated more than ₦25 billion towards the completion of the project. She described the National Library as a vital institution for preserving Nigeria’s collective memory, history and intellectual heritage. “The National Library is more than a building. It is the custodian of our collective memory, our history and our intellectual heritage. We must preserve this legacy for present and future generations,” she said. He said the government was determined to ensure that the project was completed within the approved 18-month timeline. “We are committed to ensuring uninterrupted construction, effective supervision, transparency and value for money. Nigerians deserve a National Library that meets the highest standards, and we will work to ensure that this project is delivered within the approved timeframe,” Alausa said. He charged the contractors and consultants to maintain high professional standards and ensure quality delivery. There must be no compromise on standards or the agreed completion timeline,” he added. The Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Sa’id Ahmad, described the renewed construction as an opportunity to establish a fully functional national institution capable of supporting scholarship, research and innovation. She said the project would strengthen Nigeria’s educational and intellectual development. “This renewed effort presents an important opportunity to build a fully functional National Library that will support scholarship, research and innovation. It is an investment in knowledge and in the future of our country,” she said. The National Librarian, Prof. Chinwe Veronica Nwakaego Anunobi, disclosed that the 11-storey complex covers approximately 82,941 square metres and had attained about 48 per cent completion before construction stalled. She said the scale of the project reflected its importance to the country’s information and knowledge infrastructure. “The project is a major national investment in knowledge preservation and information access. At approximately 48 per cent completion before work stopped, we now look forward to seeing the remaining construction completed so Nigerians can benefit from the facility,” Anunobi said. The Federal Ministry of Education reaffirmed its commitment to monitoring the project, ensuring accountability and maintaining quality standards throughout the construction period. The renewed commitment is expected to bring the nearly two-decade-old project closer to completion and provide Nigeria with a befitting headquarters for its national library system.
